text:
rebecca_sales: FYI -- FinTech-UK wants a POC. Two asks: 1) EU-only data path (no egress outside EU) for both inference and embeddings, 2) delta pricing for a Dedicated reserved pool in eu-west-1 vs hosted API. Any blockers?

axel_eng: quick q — when they say EU-only, do they mean control plane too or just data plane? That changes architecture.

rebecca_sales: they said control plane can be global but customer wants crypto keys and model tokens never leave EU. BYOK for KMS and tenant pinned to eu-west. Also want to understand failover: if eu-west goes down, do requests route to another region or fail with 5xx?

priya_se: we can pin tenant routing to eu-west and disable cross-region failover for the POC. That means if region is degraded, requests will failover only to a warm standby in another EU region if customer approves, otherwise they'll error. Need ops signoff for standby.

lisa_security: important: subprocessors list for EU-only can be provided but note some storage/audit vendors replicate logs to secondary regions by default. I'll attach the current subproc link and call out any non-EU processing.

rebecca_sales: pls post the link and highlight anything that touches data path. Also need clarity on egress cost calc — they want an apples-to-apples monthly estimate for 2M tokens/day.

finance_bot: @rebecca_sales rough calc: hosted API estimated token cost = ~€X/day (placeholder). Dedicated fixed monthly = base commit + usage tier. Need exact model/quantization and request distribution to be accurate.

axel_eng: infra note: for strict EU-only, recommend Dedicated or Private (VPC) — hosted still routes some control-plane telemetry through us-central telemetry collectors. If BYOK + Private control plane, we can keep all crypto ops within EU.

priya_se: config snippet we usually share for EU-pinning (example, POC config):

```
routing:
  tenant_id: fin-uk-001
  region_policy: pin
  allowed_regions: [eu-west-1]
  failover_policy: none  # options: none, eu-standby
kms:
  byok: true
  allowed_key_regions: [eu-west-1]
```

axel_eng: if they want an eu-standby failover we can set failover_policy: eu-standby and route to eu-central as secondary. That adds cross-region egress only in failover scenarios.

lisa_security: also checklist: 1) BYOK attestation, 2) subprocessors EU-only confirmation, 3) audit-log retention location, 4) network peering/CIDR exchange, 5) SLA w/ failover behavior documented. I'll start a security review ticket.

jordan_ps: timeline: we can stand up a POC tenant on Dedicated in eu-west in ~5 business days if finance ok with commitment. Private deployment (VPC) adds ~3 weeks. Which does customer prefer?

rebecca_sales: they prefer fastest path for evaluation — dedicated POC first. They asked if we can do a 1-month reserved with reduced commit for trial. Any precedent?

finance_bot: small temporary commits are possible but need approval from revenue ops; send expected throughput + duration and I'll run numbers.

priya_se: action items: @axel_eng confirm standby region options and latency estimate, @lisa_security send subproc list & any non-EU touchpoints, @finance_bot produce delta pricing (1-month reserved vs hosted) for 2M tokens/day assumptions, @jordan_ps prep Dedicated POC runbook and ETA.

axel_eng: latency note — eu-west1 primary to eu-central standby median extra hop ~12-18ms, warm standby spin-up ~30-90s depending on cache. No silent fallback unless failover enabled.

rebecca_sales: perfect. I'll bundle this into the presales reply. If we get signoff on 1-month commit, I'll kick off contract. Thanks all :tada:
